bullets.title: CPI Today Is the Deciding Factor for Sept 16 FOMC Hike; Market Pricing 63% Odds
bullets.body: JPM's Feroli forecasts Core CPI +0.21% MoM (2.4% YoY); the market is pricing ~63% probability of a 25bp hike at the Sept 16 meeting. JPM's scenario grid shows: Core ≤0.20% → SPX +1-1.5%; 0.20-0.25% → +50bp-1.25%; 0.25-0.30% → -25bp-1%; >0.30% → -1.5-2.5%. GS expects August core at +0.23% with shelter disinflation and tariff fade as tailwinds. Options are pricing ~1.0% move for the Sept 11 expiration.

bullets.title: Fed Sentiment Scores Approaching Hike-Cycle Threshold; 2-3 Hikes Priced Through 2027
bullets.body: 22V Research's Fed Sentiment Score (FRSS) shows hawkish deterioration since July's FOMC, now at levels comparable to pre-March 2022 first-hike conditions. UBS Economics revised its base case to two 25bp hikes by YE2026, up from none, following a hawkish Jackson Hole. Core PCE remains above 2% target despite sequential moderation; labor market near historical lows reinforces the case.

bullets.title: US-Iran Escalation Pushes Brent Above $100, WTI to $95; No Diplomatic Off-Ramp Visible
bullets.body: US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers overnight (eight total since Saturday), with Iran vowing a decisive response. Brent hit $100/bbl for the first time since July 24; WTI surged to ~$95. Hormuz traffic fell to six commodity vessels on Tuesday. Analysts warn a global diesel crunch will sustain elevated prices; CRB Commodities Index hit new Quad2 cycle highs. Rubber prices are up 14% in the past month, signaling core inflation pressure.

bullets.title: Dollar at 3-Month Lows; Yields at Cycle Highs; USD Weakness Accelerating Commodity Inflation
bullets.body: The USD Index hit fresh 3-month lows at $98.77 while the Japanese yen strengthened for a third consecutive session. UST 10yr yield is at 4.86% and the 2yr at 4.50%, both at tops of risk ranges. Hedgeye frames this as a 'Down Dollar = Inflation Accelerating' dynamic, with heavy corporate debt supply from AI capex buildout adding pressure. Gold bullishness reached an all-time high in Goldman's seven-year survey history.

bullets.title: Futures Soft Pre-Market: S&P -0.3–0.4%, NDX -0.4%; AI Compute Optimism Partially Offsets Geopolitical Drag
bullets.body: E-Mini S&P futures are trading down ~29-40bps, NDX -41bps, Russell -55bps. Brent above $100 and sovereign bond yields rising globally are the primary headwinds, partially offset by bullish AI conference takeaways (Astra/Muse launches, tight supply narrative). JPM maintains a Tactically Cautious/Neutral posture, recommending a barbell of +NDX vs -RTY with Mag7 favored near-term.

bullets.title: META Muse AI Agent Launches: +5% Pre-Market, #4 App Store, Usage 10x Internal Tests
bullets.body: META launched Muse, a personal AI agent capable of sending emails, booking travel, and making purchases; early usage came in 10x above testing cohorts and the app climbed to #4 on Apple's Top Downloads. META is up ~4.5-5.1% pre-market. The launch triggered a sell-off in disintermediation targets—BKNG -6.7%, SHOP -7.57%, DASH -5.3%, EXPE -8%—though JPM argues agents are designed to work with, not replace, existing platforms. Muse is free with usage limits or subscription; monetization via transaction take rates.

bullets.title: OpenAI Astra / GPT-6 Release Drives NeoCloud Rally; CRWV +11%, NBIS +7.7%, ORCL +2.4%
bullets.body: OpenAI's Astra model release drove strong momentum in AI infrastructure names Tuesday, with CRWV +11% and NBIS +7.7%. Nebius confirmed AI compute demand visibility extends to early 2028, and its shortage view has lengthened from ~18 to ~24+ months; auction-based pricing tests showed prices 15-20% above prior levels. Broadcom at Goldman's Communacopia reaffirmed AI revenue targets of $115bn FY27 and $230bn FY28 and flagged supply constraint, not semiconductor availability, as the binding bottleneck (datacenter land/power/shell).

bullets.title: TSMC N3 Shortage to Worsen in 2027: NVDA to Consume 55-60% of Wafers vs <10% in 1H26
bullets.body: JPM estimates ~600k wafers of unfulfilled N3 demand in 2026, with the gap widening in 2027 as NVDA's Rubin/Vera ramp dominates capacity (55-60% of total N3 vs <10% in 1H26). Additional demand from CPU ramps—NVDA Vera, Google Axion 2, Amazon Graviton 5, MSFT Cobalt 200—all on N3. TSMC is adding ~40% N3 capacity (Fab 18 P9 + Fab 21 P2 Arizona), but the shortage is unlikely to ease materially.

bullets.title: AI Spending Contributing 0.5-1% to US GDP; Consumer Must Slow to 1-1.5% to Respect 2% Speed Limit
bullets.body: 22V Research estimates AI will add 0.5-1% to GDP over the next two years (Morgan Stanley's narrower estimate is 0.4-0.6pp since 2025), pushing real growth well above the ~2% speed limit. To bring inflation to target, consumer spending must decelerate from 2.5%+ to 1-1.5%, but all high-frequency measures have re-accelerated post-tax-refund. Cyclical consumer stocks are down 8% YTD and -9.7% from the late July high; small caps are underperforming on elevated financial conditions index exposure.

bullets.title: AI Capex Driving Capital Markets Revenue; JPM/BAC Best Positioned; 50-55% of IB Fee Growth AI-Related
bullets.body: GS estimates AI-related activity accounts for ~50-55% of IB fee growth and ~40% of equities revenue growth in 2026, with capital markets revenue forecast to compound 4% CAGR through 2028. Large-cap banks JPM and BAC are viewed as best positioned for hyperscaler AI capex and related capital markets activity. Capex is broadening: 45% of SPX firms forecast capex growth >10% next year.

bullets.title: Apple Foldable iPhone Event Today at 1pm ET; $2K Price Point, Pro Models Up $100
bullets.body: Apple's first-ever foldable iPhone is expected to be unveiled today priced at ~$2,000, alongside iPhone 18 Pro/Max at $100 premiums vs predecessors; lower-priced models pushed to spring 2027. UBS notes AAPL has historically underperformed on event days before recovering over the following month or two. New Apple Watches and updated AirPods also on the docket.

bullets.title: QCOM-Amazon Custom Silicon Deal: $60bn Over 10 Years, Revenue Starts F1Q27
bullets.body: Qualcomm announced a multi-generation collaboration with Amazon for customized datacenter silicon, including a warrant agreement covering up to $60bn in purchases over 10 years (25M shares at $161.26, expiring 2036). Revenue begins in the December quarter. QCOM's CFO expressed 'very high confidence' in $5bn FY27 datacenter revenue; the deal is core to the $15bn FY29 target. The customer identification was already embedded in prior analyst day forecasts, so this is not incremental to the model.

bullets.title: Hedge Funds Re-Grossing at Highest Level Since Late June (+1.3z); Positioning Risk Into FOMC
bullets.body: HF gross exposure increased +1.3 standard deviations in the past week, the highest since late June, signaling active re-grossing ahead of the Sept 16 FOMC. JPM moved to Tactically Cautious/Neutral despite durable AI/macro fundamentals, citing positioning risk. EU equity put spreads are preferred as a hedge; SMID-caps likely to underperform given higher financial conditions sensitivity.

bullets.title: BOJ Set for 25bp Hike in September; ECB Near End of Cycle; Fed Behind the Curve
bullets.body: The BOJ is expected to hike 25bp at its September meeting; despite five prior hikes, its rate remains highly accommodative vs Japan's nominal GDP growth, with markets pricing three more hikes after next week. The ECB is viewed as near the end of its tightening cycle with rates already close to Eurozone nominal GDP pace. The Fed is described as 'behind the curve' given the stimulative gap between nominal growth and fed funds.

bullets.title: SaaS Multiples Compressing: IGV -0.7% YTD vs S&P +13.6%; All-SaaS at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales, All-Security at 8.2x, All-Vertical at 5.9x, with week-over-week multiple compression of 4.9%, 4.5%, and 7.5% respectively. IGV is -0.7% YTD vs the S&P +13.6%. UBS's AI Winners basket (30% fwd sales CAGR) trades at 20x P/E / 0.7x P/E-to-sales-growth vs the AI Disruption basket at 14x P/E / 2x+ ratio—a notable valuation divergence.

bullets.title: Memory Shortages Intensifying: Samsung/SK Hynix Below 10 Days of Supply; Industry Sales -10% M/M
bullets.body: Samsung and SK Hynix inventories have crashed below 10 days of supply per UBS, creating a critical shortage. Separately, JPM notes memory industry sales fell 10% M/M in July though pricing remains 'objectively strong.' Citi's TMT conference takeaway was that the memory sector (especially Asia) is the most oversold subsector, preferred over semi-cap equipment.

bullets.title: DOJ Expands Antitrust Probe into FOXA's $22B Roku Acquisition with Second Request
bullets.body: The Justice Department is expanding its antitrust inquiry into Fox's planned $22B acquisition of Roku, expected to issue a 'second request' for additional documents. The deal—$160/share ($96 cash + $64 stock)—was announced in June 2026 and targets H1 2027 close. The combined entity would become the third-largest US television player by viewing share. JPM expects the deal to ultimately close despite the probe.

bullets.title: ADBE, ORCL, RH Report Thursday After Close; ORCL Consensus $1.74 EPS / $19.13B Revenue
bullets.body: Key earnings Thursday after market close: Oracle (consensus EPS $1.74, revenue $19.13B), Adobe (consensus EPS $6.08, revenue $6.69B), and Restoration Hardware (consensus EPS $0.38, revenue $915.4M). Oracle is in focus given its AI cloud momentum (ORCL +2.36% Tuesday on Astra tailwinds) and the upcoming CRM Dreamforce/Investor Day AI metrics update.

bullets.title: US Consumer Spending Must Slow; Pre-Savings DCF Only +4.2% in 2027; Bottom Quintile Lagging
bullets.body: GS forecasts US consumer pre-savings DCF growth of +4.2% in 2027 vs +3.0% in 2026, below pre-COVID averages. The bottom income quintile is tracking only +2.8% discretionary spending growth due to elevated essential spending pressure. The 'vibe economy' shift is real: spectator sports spending +70% since 2019, gambling/membership clubs +20%, while movie theater spending is down ~33% with 248M fewer tickets sold vs 2019.

bullets.title: EU Industrial Output Contracting: France -0.8% MoM, Germany -2.3%; Euro Area Tracking -1.9% in July
bullets.body: French manufacturing fell 0.8% MoM in July (missed consensus for a modest gain), driven by transport (-2.8%) and energy-intensive sectors. Germany was worse at -2.3%. The Euro area is tracking a 1.9% MoM decline for July, with tariffs, high energy prices, and domestic political uncertainty cited as primary drivers. PMIs through August continue to signal weakness.
